outcome: Give head of quality / clinical operations director a governed method to improve major deviations identified before data lock using trial visits, protocol schedule and CRF data, with final decisions…
overview: Protocol Deviation Detection and Review addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in pharma and life sciences operations. The first proof of value uses trial visits, protocol schedule and CRF data. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is major deviations identified before data lock, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.
kpi: major deviations identified before data lock

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: trial visits, protocol schedule and CRF data; define major deviations identified before data lock and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of Quality / Clinical Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
